facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s presented with a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption that had lasted 1 month
scaly, crusted pink plaques that involved the periorbital skin
Punch biopsy from the left upper eyelid demonstrated vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy
lenalidomide (severely worsened platelet count, with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques and vacuolar interface dermatitis on biopsy is consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, a common manifestation of lupus nephritis.
The patient's periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques could be a manifestation of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, a type of skin cancer that can present with similar symptoms.

The patient's history of acute myeloid leukemia and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, combined with the presentation of a periorbital eruption with vacuolar interface dermatitis, could be consistent with graft-versus-host disease, a complication of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
The patient's history of lupus nephritis and exposure to hydroxychloroquine and lenalidomide, which can induce lupus-like symptoms, could be consistent with drug-induced lupus erythematosus.

The patient's presentation of a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques could be a manifestation of periorbital dermatitis, a common skin condition that can present with similar symptoms.

The patient's history of acute myeloid leukemia and presentation of a periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques could be consistent with leukemia cutis, a rare manifestation of leukemia that can present with skin lesions.
It explains the deep vein thrombosis finding.
It explains the immune thrombocytopenia finding.
